cases.title: Offline code-host suites pass
steps: From the repo root run: pnpm vitest run packages/adapters/src/code-host-conformance.test.ts apps/api/src/git-proxy.test.ts apps/api/src/git-push-policy.test.ts apps/api/src/git-push.integration.test.ts packages/adapters/src/code-repo-tools.test.ts packages/adapters/src/code-request-push.test.ts packages/adapters/src/code-change-request.test.ts
cases.expected: All listed test files run (git-dependent ones are not skipped on a machine with git) and pass with zero failures

cases.title: GitHub token connect validates input
steps: Start the app and create a test user as TESTING.md describes
cases.expected: Both calls fail with a 4xx error (BAD_REQUEST); neither response body contains the string placeholder-token; GET-equivalent rpc codeHosts/connections/list still returns []

cases.title: Git proxy rejects missing or bogus grants
steps: Start the app as TESTING.md describes
curl -i "$API/git/abc123.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack" with no Authorization header (use the API origin pnpm dev prints, or $WEB if it proxies /git)
cases.expected: First response is 401 with a WWW-Authenticate: Basic header; second is 403 with a text/plain body starting with 'rakazo:'; neither body contains a code-host URL or token

cases.title: GitLab token connect rejects bad URLs and new users have no connections
steps: Create a fresh test user as TESTING.md describes
cases.expected: connections/list returns {"json":[]}; connectToken fails with a 4xx error whose body does not contain placeholder-token

cases.title: Settings shows Connections with GitHub and GitLab
steps: Sign in to the web app with a test account as TESTING.md describes
Open the user menu, choose Settings, click the nav item with data-testid settings-nav-connections
cases.expected: A Connections panel is shown with add rows labelled GitHub and GitLab; choosing GitLab opens a dialog with Server URL and Token fields and a Use OAuth app switch

cases.title: Bot settings shows Repositories and the no-computer state
steps: Sign in to the web app, open a bot's panel and its Advanced tab
If the deployment's sandbox provider is none (rpc me returns sandboxProvider none), observe the Repositories group
cases.expected: A Repositories group appears after Skills; with sandboxProvider none it shows exactly 'This bot needs a computer to use repositories.' and no add control

cases.title: Binding and disconnect reject unknown ids
steps: Create a test user and get a bot id from rpc bots/list
cases.expected: Both calls return a NOT_FOUND error (HTTP 404) and bots/repositories/list for that bot still returns {"repositories":[]}
